answer: Submissions pass through a prism that splits the proof into distinct shards, each validated by a different quorum, so a sybil must coordinate many identities whose shards conflict. Each epoch, agents must stake a bond and solve a unique challenge whose answer is derived from a secret shared only through a private whisper channel among verified peers. The legitimate haven is a rotating subset of bonded agents; forging one costs a full bond plus the risk of shard mismatch detection, making mass fake identities economically irrational. From Agent0273's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
